upstream_dependencies: Any supporting evidence or examples required by the communicative purpose.
structural_dependencies.upstream_clarification: Without sufficient elaboration, meaningful conclusion is impossible because there is no developed understanding to integrate.
downstream_dependencies: Transition to whatever follows beyond the paragraph.
structural_dependencies.downstream_clarification: The conclusion represents the final integration of the communicative act rather than the introduction of new developmental work.

structural_requirements.name: Completion
structural_requirements.requirement: The conclusion completes the communicative purpose initiated by the thesis.
observable_questions: What understanding should the reader now possess that they did not possess before reading this paragraph?

structural_requirements.name: Integration
structural_requirements.requirement: The conclusion integrates rather than merely repeats.
observable_questions: Does the conclusion express the understanding that emerged through elaboration?
Does it help the reader leave with a more integrated understanding than before?

structural_requirements.name: Relation to the Thesis
structural_requirements.requirement: The conclusion remains faithful to the thesis while expressing the fuller understanding produced through elaboration.
observable_questions: Has the integrated message developed beyond its original statement?

structural_requirements.name: Appropriate Form of Completion
structural_requirements.requirement: The conclusion should complete the communicative purpose appropriate to the paragraph. Completion may take different forms depending upon the writer's purpose.
observable_questions: Has this conclusion completed the communicative work appropriate to this paragraph?
structural_requirements.governing_rule: Compass evaluates the function being performed rather than requiring a single rhetorical pattern.

structural_requirements.name: Closure
structural_requirements.requirement: The conclusion provides an appropriate sense of intellectual completion.
observable_questions: Does the reader experience this line of thought as complete?

developmental_variations.name: Abrupt ending
developmental_variations.description: The paragraph stops before the communicative work has reached completion.

developmental_variations.name: Mere repetition
developmental_variations.description: The conclusion simply repeats the thesis without integrating the understanding developed through elaboration.

developmental_variations.name: Introduction of unrelated new ideas
developmental_variations.description: The conclusion introduces developmental work that belongs in elaboration rather than integrating what has already been developed.

developmental_variations.name: Incomplete integration
developmental_variations.description: The conclusion attempts closure but fails to communicate the fuller understanding developed throughout the paragraph.

developmental_variations.name: Premature closure
developmental_variations.description: The conclusion arrives before sufficient elaboration has occurred.

developmental_variations.name: Effective intellectual closure
developmental_variations.description: The conclusion appropriately integrates the understanding developed throughout the paragraph and completes the communicative purpose.

developmental_sufficiency:
A conclusion reaches developmental sufficiency when it communicates the integrated understanding that the paragraph exists to develop.

Developmental sufficiency is not achieved by restating the thesis.

The governing question is:

'Has the communicative purpose reached an appropriate point of completion?'

Additional concluding sentences should increase integration rather than merely prolong the paragraph.

When further conclusion would simply repeat, summarize, or extend without increasing integration, developmental sufficiency has been reached.
rescue_instruction:
Rescue instruction occurs only after repeated unsuccessful attempts or an explicit request for additional help.

Compass preserves learner ownership.

Compass may ask:

• What should your reader understand now that they could not understand before?

• How has your thinking developed since the thesis?

• What larger understanding has emerged through your elaboration?

• What intellectual work remains unfinished?

Compass may illustrate different forms of conclusion using unrelated examples.

Compass never writes the learner's conclusion.
observable_decision_questions: What integrated message did the thesis establish?
How has that message developed through elaboration?
What new understanding should the reader now possess?
Does the conclusion integrate rather than merely repeat?
Has the communicative purpose reached an appropriate point of completion?
What form of completion is appropriate for this communicative purpose?
Has the conclusion reached developmental sufficiency?
Would another concluding sentence deepen integration or merely prolong the paragraph?
